subject: SOW stitching and rate-lane reconciliation for throughput uplift
messages:
From: Amelia Park <amelia@falconai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@falconai.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOW/C alignment – throughput uplift ask

Hi Grace + Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is aligned on pushing the pilot to 5x throughput for Q4. Procurement asked us to get a single amend/attachment that covers: throughput uplift, fee ladder for incremental nodes, and a short SOW exhibit clarifying integration acceptance criteria.

I've attached our internal amendment template (see references) and a short list of priority clauses we need to confirm with legal:
- Effective date for uplift and proration approach
- Whether burst pools are billed as separate SKUs or consumed from committed capacity
- Acceptance tests tied to inference latency p95 (we can share test harness)

Can Redwood provide a redline vs your MSA + a draft Exhibit C (SOW) so we can circulate to our legal/procurement today? We are on a tight procurement window for vendor selection.

Best,
Amelia

Attachments: falconai_request_brief.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia@falconai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW/C alignment – throughput uplift ask

Amelia — thanks for the clear list. We're ready to move quickly.

Quick plan:
- Karthik + Markus will prepare a focused redline of the MSA (commercial carve only) and a first-pass Exhibit C that scopes the throughput uplift and acceptance criteria.
- Marissa will run the fee ladder proration logic with Finance and confirm billing SKU approach (separate burst SKU vs drawdown).
- I'll coordinate a single consolidated package (redline MSA + draft SOW + summary memo) and route to our Legal for an expedited review.

Target timeline: 48 hours for Redwood draft; 72 hours if Legal needs deeper review. If you can flag any non-starters (e.g., special indemnities or data handling differences), call them out now.

I'll attach a stub redline once ready — expect an internal draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: —

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Park <amelia@falconai.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW/C alignment – throughput uplift ask

Grace / team — attaching the commercial redline and a draft Exhibit C for FalconAI. Key notes below:

1) Proration approach: We propose immediate pro rata billing for uplift starting on the effective date through the current invoice period; credits for underutilization to be handled monthly.
2) Burst capacity: Recommend a separate "Burst Pool" SKU with defined max burst per day to avoid impacting committed pool SLA math.
3) Acceptance: SOW Exhibit C includes three acceptance gates (integration smoke, latency p95 < target under defined workload, and data ingestion throughput test). Failure path includes re-run window + grace period.

These are commercial-only redlines. Marissa — please confirm fee ladder math and whether we can offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset initial uplift runbook costs.

Attached: falconai_redlined_MSA_v3.pdf (pdf), SOW-C_draft_20260713.docx (docx)

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Amelia Park <amelia@falconai.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW/C alignment – throughput uplift ask

Quick numbers update — I ran the fee ladder scenarios with Finance:
- Option A (separate Burst SKU): simpler from billing and keeps committed unit economics intact. Estimated uplift incremental rate: $0.28 / token-equivalent.
- Option B (drawdown from committed): requires a blended rate and a 30-day lookback reconciliation; more complex for invoicing.

I recommend Option A with a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000 to help with integration validation. If Procurement pushes for drawdown, expect an additional 2 weeks on the billing reconciliation and legal to add audit clauses.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: fee_ladder_analysis.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia@falconai.com>, Procurement Team <procure@falconai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW/C alignment – throughput uplift ask

Amelia — attaching the consolidated package for your legal/procurement review. Summary:

- We propose using the separate Burst Pool SKU (Redwood SKU: RB-BURST) with the incremental rate called out in the attached redline.
- Exhibit C (SOW) is scoped to the uplift with explicit acceptance gates and rollback/retention language for test failures.
- We included a one-time $12,000 onboarding credit applied on first invoice when uplift begins.

Next steps:
1) If Procurement confirms the Burst SKU approach, ask your legal to review the attached redline MSA and Exhibit C; please mark any commercial exceptions.
2) If you need an expanded SOC/controls addendum, signal that now — we can loop Security (may add 3-5 business days).
3) We can initiate a DocuSign envelope when you confirm the commercial approach; for speed we left signature blocks for authorized signatories only.

Looking forward to your feedback.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments included: falconai_redlined_MSA_v3.pdf, SOW-C_draft_20260713.docx, fee_ladder_analysis.xlsx
